lineage.strategy: Shift from historical growth evidence to current financing structure and contracted-capacity evidence that addresses execution funding and concentration risk.

observations.fact: Nebius entered a roughly $775 million senior secured facility backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows, maturing October 31, 2030 at SOFR plus 2.50%; the company states contracted cash flows plus the facility cover more than 100% of capex for the underlying deployment.

Nebius disclosed a five-year agreement to provide Meta $12 billion of dedicated capacity beginning in early 2027, plus a Meta commitment to purchase additional available compute capacity up to $15 billion over five years under specified conditions.

risks.risk: The financing is secured by GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows, increasing asset encumbrance, while the very large Meta relationship creates material customer-concentration and delivery-execution exposure.

unknowns.unknown: Issuer releases do not establish realized margins or return on invested capital for the new contracted deployments; delivery and utilization economics remain to be proven.

recommendation: Use the secured financing terms and contracted-capacity commitments as source-addressed execution inputs; explicitly haircut for concentration, leverage and unproven realized deployment returns.
